title: Trumpet
reference_instrument: University of Iowa MIS Bb trumpet (Bach 180S37 Stradivarius, 1987, per MISBbtrumpet.html)
summary: Limits: two routes that cannot be combined (G3, Bb3, E4 on a linear bore with a flanged modal bell; F4, Bb4, D5 on a nonlinear gas bore with a piston bell); valves only as derived loops for E4 and G3; no A5; too dark on the modal-bell pages (centroid 613 to 801 Hz, recordings 1344 to 1393 Hz). A Bb trumpet played by a lip valve: the note is the lock the loop finds, and no pitch is an input. Bore: the 34-station profile of Tournemenne and Chabassier (2019). Lip: Cullen's (2000) embouchure 19, a trombone-rig artificial lip, not a trumpeter's. Mouth pressure: a 14 kPa attack, then 3.5 x 7 Pa/Hz x the note (Fletcher and Tarnopolsky 1999); each pre-stress is a player's setting chosen from a first render's pitch. Flow noise at the lips (Oldham and Ukpoho 1990, extrapolated) is on the modal-bell pages and Bb4. A stand-in bore, not the recorded Bach 180S37's.
physics_present: fs-couple brass_loop: a one-degree-of-freedom outward-striking lip (Cullen 2000, embouchure 19: resonance 237 Hz, quality factor 12, inverse mass 0.072 m2/kg, 9 mm wide, 0.25 mm rest gap; the width and gap are her own estimates) with a Bernoulli aperture solved implicitly with the mouthpiece junction. Blowing pressure and lip pre-stress are gestures on the shared canonical schedule
The bore: the 34-station profile published with Tournemenne and Chabassier (2019), copied from the openwind example file, 1.4187 m long, valves straightened

G3, Bb3 and E4: a linear multimodal transfer-matrix bore with viscothermal loss, a flanged modal radiation load at the bell (modal_baffle), and the listener by a finite-distance Rayleigh integral over every mouth mode, 1.524 m on axis. The mouth-flow ladder runs at a declared tail tolerance of 2e-6 (mouth_flow_tail_tol on the card)
F4, Bb4 and D5: a nonlinear Euler gas bore with Zwikker-Kosten wall memory (64 poles, 20 to 8000 Hz), a baffled-piston bell at the bore end and dry air from the thermochemical gas packs

Flow noise at the lips on G3, Bb3, E4 and Bb4 (the constriction_noise row): a pressure source in each third octave, sized by the blowing pressure and the cup radius of the card's own first bore record, from the printed law of Oldham and Ukpoho (1990, as reprinted by Guedel 2005). It is an extrapolation from dampers and plates in a large duct at 10 to 25 m/s, and no level was set. F4 and D5 carry none yet

Two valve notes: E4 adds the second valve's loop (84.36 mm) and G3 a three-semitone loop (268.4 mm), each the bore's 1.4187 m times the equal-tempered length ratio, inserted as straight tube. The lengths are derived, not measured
The fanfare and the slur are one render each on the modal-bell route with the flow-noise row on, so every note change happens inside the simulation
physics_missing: Valves: only E4's second-valve loop and G3's three-semitone loop exist, as straight tube of derived length with none of a real valve's bends or port steps. Every other valve and combination, the tuning slide and valve switching during a note are absent, and the cards hold no measured loop length for this trumpet

A5: no hold on the second-valve bore lands on it. At 21.56 kPa, pre-stress 2.56, 2.62 and 2.68 sound the sixth partial, E5; a slur up from pre-stress 2.0 to 2.62 starts on the fifth partial, jumps to E5 and stays there, never reaching A5. A slow sweep of the lip reached A5 only by climbing through every partial, so the lock depends on the path. The A5 page stays recording-only

The two routes cannot be joined: the flanged modal bell needs a linear bore, so the modal-bell pages (G3, Bb3, E4) have no gas nonlinearity, no wave steepening and no wall-material memory, and the gas-bore pages (F4, Bb4, D5) radiate through a piston bell. Each page says which it lacks
Brightness on the modal-bell pages: the centroids are 613 Hz (E4), 769 Hz (G3) and 801 Hz (Bb3) against the recordings' 1383, 1344 and 1393 Hz, and E4's ninth harmonic nearly vanishes

The shape of the flow noise: the row has no frequency shape of its own. On Bb3 the floor between the harmonics is 4 and 6 dB under the recording at 0.5 to 1 and 1 to 2 kHz and 6 and 23 dB over it at 2 to 4 and 4 to 6.9 kHz. The law is an extrapolation from a large duct to a mouthpiece, and no level was set against any recording

A trumpeter's lip: the lip is an artificial latex lip measured on a trombone-size mouthpiece, its outward-striking mode only, with channel width and rest gap that are not a trumpeter's. No trumpet-player lip set is published. The trumpet cards carry no lip_area_exponent line, so the aperture area is width times gap

The recorded instrument: the Iowa trumpet is a Bach 180S37 and no numeric bore of it was found, so the bore is a population stand-in. That the stations were measured from a real commercial trumpet is as reported and not verified here, and the mouthpiece is the station table's cup and throat, not a named one

Intonation: the stand-in bore's own resonances are not on the equal-tempered series, so each note's pre-stress is chosen from the emergent pitch of a first render. How a real Bach 180S37 would sit is unknown

Radiation and room: the receiver is a flanged half-space point 1.524 m on axis. The directivity of a real unflanged bell, the player's bell orientation and any room are not modelled. The modal-bell pages run at 32 kHz in the engine, and the comparison is valid only below 6.9 kHz

The bore gas on the modal-bell pages is dry air at 293.15 K (the card's ambient line) and the propagation is linear. Breath-warmed and humidified gas, wall vibration, mutes, vibrato and the player's tonguing beyond the pressure gestures are not modelled
